title: Crispy Corn-Zucchini Fritters with Jalapeño-Lime Yogurt
dek: Golden-edged zucchini and sweet-corn fritters with feta, scallions, and a cool, punchy jalapeño-lime yogurt.
image_alt: Golden zucchini fritters plated with leafy salad and a creamy dip
ingredients: 2 medium zucchini (about 1 lb), grated on the large holes of a box grater
1 1/2 cups corn kernels, from 2 ears or thawed from frozen
1 small jalapeño, seeded and finely chopped, divided
1/4 cup avocado or other neutral high-heat oil, plus more as needed
4 cups lightly dressed arugula or mixed greens, for serving, optional

instructions.name: Drain the zucchini
instructions.text: Toss the grated zucchini with 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt in a colander and let it stand 10 minutes. Transfer it to a clean kitchen towel and squeeze firmly over the sink until no more liquid drips out. You should have about 1 1/2 packed cups.

instructions.name: Mix the jalapeño-lime yogurt
instructions.text: Stir the Greek yogurt with the lime zest, 1 tablespoon lime juice, garlic, half of the jalapeño, 1 tablespoon cilantro, and a pinch of the remaining salt. Refrigerate while the fritters cook.

instructions.name: Build the fritter batter
instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, flour, cornmeal, baking powder, cumin, black pepper, and remaining salt into a thick batter. Fold in the squeezed zucchini, corn, scallions, feta, remaining cilantro, and remaining jalapeño. Let the batter rest 5 minutes so the cornmeal can hydrate.

instructions.name: Heat the skillet
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat until shimmering, about 2 minutes. Scoop four packed 1/4-cup portions into the skillet and flatten each to a 3-inch round about 1/2 inch thick.

instructions.name: Fry until crisp
instructions.text: Cook 3 to 4 minutes per side until deeply golden, firm in the center, and at least 160°F on an instant-read thermometer. Transfer to a wire rack set over a sheet pan. Add the remaining oil as needed and cook the second batch; reduce the heat if the crumbs darken before the centers set.

instructions.name: Serve
instructions.text: Season the hot fritters with a small pinch of salt. Serve two per person with the jalapeño-lime yogurt, extra lime wedges, and dressed greens if using.

why_it_works: Salting and aggressively squeezing the zucchini removes the water that otherwise makes fritters limp and gummy.
Cornmeal absorbs lingering moisture and creates a crisp, craggy edge without requiring a heavy flour batter.
Resting cooked fritters on a rack preserves both crisp sides; paper towels trap steam against the bottom.
swaps: Replace feta with shredded sharp cheddar, crumbled goat cheese, or omit it for a dairy-free fritter.
Use thawed frozen corn when fresh corn is unavailable; blot it dry before adding it to the batter.
For less heat, omit the jalapeño and add 2 tablespoons finely chopped roasted red pepper to the batter.
storage: Refrigerate fritters and yogurt separately in airtight containers for up to 4 days. Reheat fritters on a rack in a 400°F oven for 8 to 10 minutes, or air-fry at 375°F for 4 to 6 minutes, until crisp and 165°F in the center. Freeze cooked fritters between parchment sheets for up to 2 months; thaw overnight before reheating.
notes: Measure the squeezed zucchini rather than the raw shreds; very large zucchini can hold substantially more water.
Keep the oil near 350°F if using a thermometer. Cooler oil makes greasy fritters, while overly hot oil burns the outside before the egg sets.
The batter should hold its shape on a spoon. If it puddles, fold in 1 additional tablespoon flour.

faqs.q: Can I bake the zucchini fritters instead of frying them?
faqs.a: Yes. Brush a parchment-lined sheet pan with 1 tablespoon oil, shape the fritters, brush their tops lightly with more oil, and bake at 425°F for 12 minutes. Flip and bake 8 to 10 minutes more, until browned and 160°F in the center.

faqs.q: Why are my fritters falling apart?
faqs.a: The usual causes are wet zucchini or flipping too soon. Squeeze the zucchini until very dry, pack each scoop, and wait until a firm brown crust forms before turning it.

faqs.q: Can I mix the batter ahead?
faqs.a: For the crispest result, mix it no more than 30 minutes before cooking because salted vegetables keep releasing water. The yogurt sauce can be made up to 3 days ahead.

title: Sheet-Pan Dill Pork Tenderloin with Crispy Smashed Potatoes
dek: Juicy mustard-glazed pork tenderloin, crackly smashed potatoes, and blistered green beans finished with fresh dill on one sheet pan.
image_alt: Sliced roasted pork tenderloin with potatoes and green vegetables
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb baby gold potatoes, each no larger than 1 1/2 inches
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided, plus more for the potato water
1 pork tenderloin (1 1/4 to 1 1/2 lb), silver skin removed
12 oz green beans, trimmed and thoroughly dried

instructions.name: Parboil the potatoes
instructions.text: Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the upper-middle position. Put the potatoes in a saucepan, cover with cold water by 1 inch, season the water generously with salt, and bring to a boil. Simmer 12 to 15 minutes, until a paring knife slides in with slight resistance. Drain well and let steam-dry 5 minutes.

instructions.name: Mix the glaze
instructions.text: Stir the Dijon, maple syrup, garlic, smoked paprika, 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, 2 tablespoons dill, and 1 teaspoon finely grated lemon zest. Reserve 1 tablespoon of this clean glaze in a small bowl before it touches the raw pork.

instructions.name: Smash and start the potatoes
instructions.text: Place the potatoes on a heavy rimmed half-sheet pan and flatten each to about 1/2 inch thick with the bottom of a sturdy glass. Drizzle with 1 tablespoon oil and season with 1/2 teaspoon salt and the remaining black pepper. Roast 15 minutes.

instructions.name: Add the pork and beans
instructions.text: Pat the pork dry and coat it all over with the larger portion of glaze. Carefully remove the hot pan, turn the potatoes, and clear the center for the pork. Toss the green beans and shallot with the remaining 1 tablespoon oil and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt; arrange them around the pork without covering the potatoes.

instructions.name: Roast to temperature
instructions.text: Return the pan to the oven and roast 16 to 22 minutes, turning the pork once after 10 minutes, until its thickest part reaches 145°F and the beans are blistered. Transfer the pork to a board immediately. If the vegetables need more color, return the pan to the oven while the meat rests.

instructions.name: Rest and finish
instructions.text: Rest the pork at least 3 minutes, then brush with the reserved clean glaze and slice across the grain into 1/2-inch medallions. Squeeze half the lemon over the beans and potatoes, scatter with the remaining dill, and serve with lemon wedges.

why_it_works: Parboiling gelatinizes the potato surfaces; smashing exposes more of that starchy surface to the hot pan for crisp edges.
Adding the pork after the potatoes get a head start keeps the lean tenderloin juicy while the potatoes still become deeply browned.
A measured 145°F pull temperature followed by a three-minute rest gives safe, moist pork instead of dry slices.
swaps: Use broccoli florets or thin asparagus instead of green beans; add asparagus only for the final 10 to 12 minutes.
Substitute whole-grain mustard for Dijon for a coarser glaze, or honey for the maple syrup.
If using two smaller tenderloins, begin checking both at 14 minutes and remove each one as it reaches 145°F.
storage: Refrigerate pork and vegetables in a shallow airtight container for up to 4 days. Reheat the potatoes and beans on a sheet pan at 400°F for 8 to 10 minutes. Add pork slices for only the final 3 to 4 minutes and heat leftovers to 165°F so the lean meat does not dry out. Freeze sliced pork for up to 2 months; potatoes are best refrigerated rather than frozen.
notes: Pork tenderloin is the narrow, boneless cut, not the much larger pork loin; the two require different cooking times.
Dry green beans and potatoes brown better. Water on their surfaces creates steam and softens the potato edges.
Reserve finishing glaze before brushing the raw meat to avoid cross-contamination. Discard any glaze or utensil that touched raw pork.

faqs.q: Is pork safe if it is slightly pink?
faqs.a: Color is not a reliable doneness test. Whole-muscle pork is safe when its thickest part reaches 145°F and then rests for at least 3 minutes; a faint pink center can remain at that temperature.

faqs.q: Can I skip boiling the potatoes?
faqs.a: Not for the same texture and timing. Raw potatoes take longer to soften and will not smash cleanly. You can parboil them up to 2 days ahead, refrigerate them dry, and continue with the recipe when ready.

faqs.q: What if my tenderloin is done before the potatoes?
faqs.a: Move the pork to a board as soon as it reaches 145°F. Tent it loosely and let the potatoes roast 5 to 8 minutes longer; the pork can rest that long without becoming cold.

title: Sicilian Tuna Pasta with Burst Tomatoes, Capers & Crispy Breadcrumbs
dek: A fast Mediterranean pantry pasta with olive-oil tuna, jammy tomatoes, briny capers, lemon, and garlicky toasted breadcrumbs.
image_alt: Tomato tuna pasta twirled in a white bowl with herbs and grated topping
ingredients: 1 1/4 tsp kosher salt, divided, plus more for the pasta water
1/4 tsp red pepper flakes, plus more to taste
1 pint cherry or grape tomatoes, halved
2 cans oil-packed tuna (5 oz each), drained into a bowl and broken into large flakes
1/4 cup pitted Castelvetrano or Kalamata olives, roughly chopped, optional

instructions.name: Start the pasta water
instructions.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Salt it until pleasantly seasoned, add the pasta, and cook until 1 minute shy of the package's al dente time. Before draining, reserve 1 1/2 cups pasta water.

instructions.name: Toast the breadcrumbs
instructions.text: While the water heats, warm 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add panko, one-quarter of the sliced garlic, and a pinch of salt. Stir 3 to 4 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. Transfer immediately to a bowl and stir in half the lemon zest.

instructions.name: Burst the tomatoes
instructions.text: Return the skillet to medium-high heat with the remaining 3 tablespoons olive oil. Add the remaining garlic and red pepper flakes; cook 30 seconds. Add tomatoes, capers, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, and the olives if using. Cook 6 to 8 minutes, stirring and pressing some tomatoes, until glossy and jammy.

instructions.name: Emulsify the sauce
instructions.text: Add the drained pasta and 3/4 cup reserved pasta water to the skillet. Toss vigorously with tongs over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes until the starchy water and oil form a sauce that clings to the noodles. Add more pasta water 2 tablespoons at a time if it looks dry.

instructions.name: Fold in the tuna
instructions.text: Remove the skillet from the heat. Gently fold in the tuna, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, remaining lemon zest, parsley, and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt. Taste and add more lemon, red pepper, or a spoonful of the reserved tuna oil as needed.

instructions.name: Finish with crunch
instructions.text: Divide among warm bowls and top generously with the garlicky breadcrumbs. Serve immediately, passing any remaining breadcrumbs at the table.

why_it_works: Oil-packed tuna has a richer texture and its reserved oil can reinforce the sauce without introducing another flavor.
Starchy pasta water binds the tomato juices and olive oil into a glossy sauce instead of leaving oil at the bottom of the bowl.
Adding tuna off the heat preserves large tender flakes, while breadcrumbs provide the salty crunch usually supplied by grated cheese.
swaps: Use good-quality water-packed tuna and add 1 extra tablespoon olive oil when folding it into the pasta.
Replace tuna with canned sardines or mackerel for a stronger seafood flavor, or use drained chickpeas for a vegetarian version.
Substitute crushed canned tomatoes for fresh: use 1 cup and simmer until thickened before adding the pasta.
storage: Refrigerate pasta for up to 3 days and keep extra breadcrumbs in a separate airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days. Reheat pasta in a skillet with 2 tablespoons water per serving until it reaches 165°F, then add the breadcrumbs after heating. This dish is not ideal for freezing because the pasta and tuna can become dry.
notes: Drain the tuna into a bowl rather than the sink so its flavorful oil remains available for adjusting the finished sauce.
Capers and tuna vary in saltiness. The measured salt assumes drained capers; taste before adding more at the end.
Do not rinse the pasta. Its surface starch is essential for emulsifying the sauce in the skillet.

faqs.q: Will the tuna pasta taste overly fishy?
faqs.a: Oil-packed tuna folded in off the heat is savory but not aggressive. Lemon, parsley, tomato, and capers keep the flavor bright; choose solid light tuna for a milder result.

faqs.q: Can I make this without breadcrumbs?
faqs.a: Yes. Omit them and finish with toasted sliced almonds or pine nuts for crunch, or serve the pasta without a crunchy topping. Avoid Parmesan if you want to keep the traditional seafood-and-cheese separation.

faqs.q: Can I serve this pasta cold?
faqs.a: It is best hot, when the sauce is emulsified. For a cold version, cook short pasta, cool it on a sheet pan, and loosen the sauce with an extra tablespoon each of olive oil and lemon juice before folding everything together.
